A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamicCut/DynamicCutMix study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and matchable despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original memorization-dynamics, sample-removal, mitigation, utility, ablation and transferability experiments in Sections 3–6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Mixup comparisons, sensitivity experiments, statistical tests and computational timings.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 retains early Mem-AUC collection, averaging the top 10% of epoch scores, pruning the highest-scoring samples with default p = 0.1, and subsequent retraining. DynamicCutMix still combines filtering with TabCutMix. The new Algorithm 1 documents this existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult, Default and Shoppers, with Cardio and Wilt already covered in v2 Appendix A.2 and retained in v3 Appendix B.3. The additions introduce no new datasets, tasks or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds Mixup as an evaluated comparator under TabDDPM on Default, Shoppers and Adult in Table 12. The existing SMOTE, TabCutMix and TabCutMixPlus comparisons and generative backbones are retained.

E3.justification: Table 6 adds pruning ratios of 1% and 3% to the existing 5%, 10% and 20% sweep. New Table 7 evaluates warm-up windows of 600/700/800 epochs on Default and 2000/2100/2200 on Shoppers. Existing benchmark splits, generation counts and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens supplementary analysis through new warm-up-window sensitivity tests, expanded pruning ablations, quantitative forgetting-time comparisons, computational-overhead analysis and an aggregate privacy–utility assessment. Existing pooling, transferability, feature-quality and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly reports Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests and p-values comparing Top and Non-Top forgetting-time distributions. Both versions already average benchmark results over five independent runs and report values with ± terms; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark tables retain their values. New results cover Mixup, additional pruning ratios, warm-up windows, KS statistics, timings and aggregate averages. For example, new Table 7 reports Default memorization ratios of 15.79% at 600 warm-up epochs and 19.10% at 800; these are different settings, not a version-to-version performance decline.

T1.justification: Appendix B.8 newly presents asymptotic monitoring and top-k computation costs and compares them with backbone training cost under T much smaller than E. The distance-ratio, Mem-AUC and memorization-event definitions remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: concentrated and early sample-level memorization, DynamicCut filtering, combination with TabCutMix, utility preservation and transferability across generative models.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the easy-to-fit-region explanation in Section 4.2 with a convergence-speed interpretation, characterizes pruning and warm-up choices as empirical and dataset-dependent, and replaces the explicit overhead limitation with an argument for modest cost. Appendix B.10 also acknowledges that TCMP slightly outperforms DCM on Adult memorization.

D1.justification: v3 discloses monitoring every ten epochs, warm-up lengths, per-evaluation and total monitoring times, and baseline training times. It changes the declared code location from an anonymous repository to GitHub. Table 13 changes Wilt's reported total from 4,839 to 4,889 while retaining the split counts; this does not establish changed data usage.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Mixup, Data Shapley, online hard-example mining and self-paced learning. Appendix C.2 newly connects memorization heterogeneity to data valuation and hard samples. The main related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Observation paragraphs throughout Sections 3, 4 and 6 and the appendices are extensively rewritten with descriptive headings. v3 also expands the appendix organization, introduces pseudocode presentation, adds acknowledgments and revises the journal front matter, while largely retaining the scientific narrative.

P2.justification: Journal reformatting changes typography, margins, author layout and float placement. Figure 1 is redrawn and rescaled, adding a TabDDPM panel for already reported comparisons; Figure 4 changes from side-by-side to stacked panels. Algorithm 1 and Tables 7, 11 and 12 are added, and Table 6 gains rows.

improvement.justification: The added warm-up sensitivity evidence, Mixup comparison, statistical analysis and implementation details address specific empirical and reproducibility gaps without changing the main results. The gain is limited by imprecise new interpretations: Appendix B.9 claims best or tied-best overall Trend performance for DCM, although Table 11 reports 85.05 versus TCM's 85.46. The added overhead percentages also use total time rather than the stated baseline denominator. Overall, the additional evidence provides a modest quality improvement.
